quarters.title: Making the next owner clear
quarters.focus: Make ownership visible without asking volunteers to learn another application.
actions: I traced the existing routes, drafted a shared request list and facilitated the first reviews. I revised the list after coordinators found its status labels unclear.
quarters.tension: Requests crossed between the front desk, events and facilities; the next owner was often implicit.
quarters.style: Used the team's existing spreadsheet so the trial did not depend on a new tool. Separated the next owner from the person who first received the request. Removed a priority field after the team interpreted its labels differently.
questions: Which parts of the review remained in use later in the year?

quarters.title: A guide tested at the front desk
quarters.focus: Put the routine steps in one place while keeping escalation routes visible.
actions: I grouped the questions, drafted the guide and observed the trial. I rewrote the room-booking instructions when volunteers could not tell which exceptions needed a coordinator.
quarters.tension: Existing notes were spread across documents, and the shared desk computer was not always available.
quarters.style: Organized the guide around tasks, rather than the team's internal structure. Kept policy exceptions beside the relevant steps. Used a printable format because the shared desk computer was not always available.

quarters.title: An equipment log still in progress
quarters.focus: Test whether a simple checkout history would answer the team's everyday questions.
actions: I sketched the flow and built a local prototype. I have not connected it to real records or arranged a user trial.
quarters.tension: The library lacked a shared equipment record; a user trial and maintenance ownership were still undecided.
quarters.style: Used fictional test items during prototyping. Kept the first version limited to checkout and return. Left reminders out until the team decides who would own follow-up.
questions: Would a shared paper log solve the problem more simply?
